no adjective

not any

also no one (thing), not a single, no news

classical

Gell. 17.8.5: nūllum inde ībat oleum
Plin. NH 9.42: nūllum animal graviōre somnō premitur
Traupman 351

nūllus, nūlla, nūllum

adjective; gen. nūllīus, dat. nūllī · Declension on Wiktionary

no, not any

“No” before a noun. “And no” is nec ūllus (see any); with persons, “no one” is nēmō; “no …” of a quantity is often nihil with a genitive (below).

Other words

  • nihil + gen. — no (amount of): no news, no warmth

    indeclinable pronoun with a partitive genitive · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 12.1.2: novī nihil; Liv. 21.54.8: nihil calōris inerat

    For “no” before a mass or abstract noun: nihil novī, no news; nihil calōris, no warmth (see nothing).

Examples

  • nūllum inde ībat oleum

    no oil came out of itGell. 17.8.5

  • sī rem nūllam habēbis, quod in buccam vēnerit scrībitō

    if you have no news, write whatever comes into your mouthCic. Att. 1.12.4

  • nūllum animal graviōre somnō premitur

    no animal sleeps more heavilyPlin. NH 9.42

  • sōl fervit, et fit nihil; it diēs, et amīcī nūllī eunt

    the sun blazes and nothing happens; the day goes by, and no friends comeGell. 2.29.10

  • nōn captō ante cibō, nōn ope ūllā ad arcendum frīgus adhibitā, nihil calōris inerat

    they had eaten nothing beforehand and had nothing to keep out the cold, so there was no warmth in themLiv. 21.54.8

See also any, none, nothing, zero.
